actions.name: Distributed Warzone RAT as malicious email attachment
actions.description: Warzone RAT was primarily distributed as a malicious attachment in an email, either through broad malware spam campaigns or targeted phishing attempts.

actions.name: Distributed Warzone RAT via malicious Microsoft Office files
actions.description: Warzone RAT was often distributed with or through malicious Microsoft Office files exploiting CVE-2017-11882.

actions.name: Warzone RAT gains persistence by copying itself and creating registry key
actions.description: During installation, the malware gains persistence by copying itself to C:\Users\User\AppData\Roaming\ and creating a registry key with a value set to the location of Warzone’s executable binary to enable automatic execution after reboot.

actions.name: Warzone RAT communicates with C2 servers via TCP over port 5200
actions.description: The malware communicates with C2 servers via TCP over a configurable port which defaults to port 5200, using encrypted payloads with RC4 encryption.

actions.name: Warzone RAT collects and sends basic system information to C2 server
actions.description: After decrypting communication and connecting with the C2 server, the malware collects basic system information such as PC name and operating system and sends it back to the C2 server.
